children: "I think the lack of actionable news out of the U.S.-China trade summit has led to somewhat of a 'buyers strike' through the morning," says Oliver Sloup of Blue Line Futures. Sloup adds that rumors of discussions between the U.S. and Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz are also a factor in trading, but the effect of these discussions on futures movements may be small. "It seems to be setting up for a 'boy that cried wolf' scenario, where we keep getting these headlines and they don't amount to much," says Sloup. Most-active corn falls 0.6%, soybeans slide 0.5%, and wheat drops 0.7%. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)
